title: Ankhorage Repository
summary: Connects an application project to a source repository through portable manifests, local snapshot boundaries, and GitHub provider operations.
purpose: Provide an independently usable repository capability that can inspect, create, and synchronize project source without coupling application logic to one source-control mechanism.
responsibilities: Read project snapshots and persist portable repository connection manifests.
Coordinate repository connection through explicit source-provider gateways.
Expose GitHub authentication, inventory, creation, inspection, and synchronization operations through public package boundaries.
boundaries: Does not own application authoring, deployment, or organization-wide package indexing.
Does not embed repository credentials in portable manifests.
Does not require GitHub when a different repository gateway is supplied.
audience: Applications and tooling that connect a project directory to a source repository.
useCases: Create a missing GitHub repository and publish a project's source snapshot.
Inspect repository readiness before connecting an application project.
Enumerate repositories available to an authenticated GitHub user.

architecture.role: Repository capability owner coordinating portable connection policy with replaceable local-state and source-provider ports.
invariants: Portable repository manifests contain no live credentials or provider client objects.
GitHub-specific transport and authentication stay at provider adapter boundaries.
Project snapshots and manifests are accessed through explicit ports suitable for standalone use.

configuration: GitHub operations require explicit authentication with the scopes needed for the requested repository action.
security: Repository credentials remain request-scoped provider inputs and are not persisted in portable repository manifests.
